name: Gaming Video Ideas
blurb: 45 gaming video and Shorts ideas with hooks, from clips to sketches you can film at home
title: 45 Gaming Video Ideas and Gaming Shorts Ideas (With Hooks)
description: 45 gaming video ideas for Shorts and YouTube: gameplay clips, guides, setup tours and gamer sketches, each with a 2-second hook and format. Check game policies.
h1: 45 Gaming Video Ideas, Each With a Hook and Format
answer: This list is for gamers who want to make Shorts or longer videos about the games they play. Each idea says what to film, the hook for the first two seconds and the format; before you post gameplay, check that game's video or content policy, and only use games you own legitimately.

items.d: Cut your single best play with a short caption. Hook: the moment itself, starting one second before it lands. Format: gameplay clip with captions.
Share your funniest mistake with honest commentary. Hook: the moment right before it goes wrong. Format: gameplay with voice-over.
Show a tense situation and pause before the outcome. Hook: the low health bar or timer. Format: gameplay with a freeze frame.
Show your fastest attempt with a timer on screen. Hook: the timer starting. Format: gameplay.

sections.h: How to pick and film a gaming video
body: Pick the games you genuinely play and know well. Viewers come back for your voice and your take, so a clear opinion or a useful tip beats a generic clip.

ol: Check the game publisher's video or content policy before posting gameplay, and follow it.
Choose one idea and find the single moment the video is built around.
Record gameplay with your platform's built-in capture or free software, and your voice close to the microphone.
Cut to the moment fast, add captions, and keep Shorts under 60 seconds.
Post on a rhythm you can keep and turn ideas that land into a series.

body.note: Do not use pirated games, cracks or leaked builds, and do not reupload other creators' clips. Use only music you have the rights to.

ul: Start one second before the big moment, not at the menu.
Show the result first: the win screen, then how you got there.
Put the rule or challenge in big text over the first frame.
Freeze before the outcome and ask viewers to guess.
Open on a problem every player knows, like a low health bar.
Begin with your strongest opinion in the first line.
Use a familiar game interface joke over a real-life scene.

faq.q: Am I allowed to post gameplay from any game?
faq.a: It depends on the publisher. Many allow it with conditions, some restrict monetisation or certain content. Read each game's video policy before posting, and follow your platform's rules.

faq.q: Can I make gaming videos without gameplay?
faq.a: Yes. Setup tours, sketches like The Group Project and talking-head opinions need no footage. The linked scripts are free under CC BY 4.0 with the credit Script: cv.cm.
It is optional. Voice-over with captions works well for guides; a face cam adds reactions to clips. Try both and keep the one you enjoy making.
